fields.summary: User can reset their password via an emailed link
fields.description:
As a registered user I want to reset my password through a link sent to my email so that I can regain access when I forget it.

Project Key: SMOKE
Issue ID (numeric): 10001

Acceptance Criteria:
1. Submitting a registered email address on the 'Forgot password' form sends an email with a single-use password-reset link that is valid for 60 minutes.
2. Opening a reset link more than 60 minutes after it was sent shows the message 'This reset link has expired' and a 'Request a new link' button.

attachments.reset-policy.md:
Password reset policy
- A reset link stays valid for 60 minutes.
- At most 3 reset requests per account per hour.

test_cases.name: Password reset via single-use link valid for 60 minutes
test_cases.objective: Verify that submitting a registered email address sends a single-use password-reset link valid for 60 minutes, the password can be reset, and the link cannot be reused.
test_cases.precondition: A user account with the email 'user@example.com' is registered in the system, and access to the corresponding email inbox is available.
test_cases.review_comments:
Test case review

Review iterations: 2, stop reason: iteration_limit.

  • [HIGH] unactioned expected result (AC-1): In Step 4, the expected result asserts that the user can successfully log in with the new password and that authentication with the previous password fails, but the step's action only covers submitting the new password form. Expected results must be directly caused by the action of that step; asserting login outcomes without performing the corresponding login actions leads to inconsistent execution by testers who lack instructions on how and where to verify authentication.
    Suggested fix: Retain only the reset confirmation message check in Step 4's expected result, and add subsequent actions/steps to navigate to the login screen, attempt login with the previous password to verify authentication failure, and log in with the new password to verify successful authentication.

Duplicate check

No duplicate test cases found.

test_cases.name: Expired password reset link handling after 60 minutes
test_cases.objective: Verify that opening a password-reset link more than 60 minutes after it was sent displays an expiration message and that clicking 'Request a new link' redirects to the 'Forgot password' form.
test_cases.precondition: A password-reset email has been generated and sent to the user, and more than 60 minutes have elapsed since the link was issued.
test_cases.review_comments:
Test case review

Review iterations: 2, stop reason: iteration_limit.

  • [HIGH] imprecise expected result (AC-2): In step 2, the expected result states that 'the URL path reflects the forgot password page', which is vague and lacks an explicit URL path (e.g. '/forgot-password'). This ambiguity allows testers to verify redirection inconsistently or overlook routing defects.
    Suggested fix: Update the expected result of step 2 to specify the concrete expected URL path (e.g. '/forgot-password') rather than using the generic phrase 'the URL path reflects the forgot password page'.

Duplicate check

No duplicate test cases found.

test_cases.name: Password reset request rate limit of 3 requests per account per hour
test_cases.objective: Verify that a registered user can submit up to 3 password reset requests per account within an hour, and that attempting a 4th request within the same one-hour window is throttled or rejected with a rate limit message and no email sent.
test_cases.precondition: A user account with the email 'user@example.com' is registered in the system, and access to the corresponding email inbox is available.
test_cases.review_comments:
Test case review

Review iterations: 2, stop reason: iteration_limit.

  • [HIGH] ambiguous step (AC-1): Step 3 is the weakest step of the test case: its action states 'Submit another password reset request for the registered email address within the specified time window', but it omits the necessary interactions to reach and submit the form again (navigating back to the 'Forgot password' page and entering the email address) after Step 2 ended on a confirmation notification. In addition, the action refers to 'the specified time window', but Step 3's test data omits any time constraint parameter relative to the first request. Consequently, testers may execute the step inconsistently or fail to execute the 4th attempt within the 1-hour rate limit window.
    Suggested fix: Update Step 3 action to: 'Navigate to the 'Forgot password' page, enter the registered email address into the input field, and submit the 4th password reset request within the specified time window from the first request.' and add 'time window: within 60 minutes of the first request' to Step 3 test data.
  • [HIGH] missing precondition (AC-1): The test case preconditions verify a rate limit of at most 3 requests per account per hour, but do not state that the account has not requested any password resets within the past 60 minutes. If prior reset requests occurred for 'user@example.com' in the hour before testing, Step 2 will trigger rate limiting prematurely, causing false test failures and inconsistent execution.
    Suggested fix: Add a precondition stating: 'The registered user account has no password reset requests recorded within the last 60 minutes (rate limit counter is reset).'

Duplicate check

No duplicate test cases found.
